domains.name: Circular and Rotational Motion in Daily Life
Aerodynamics and Air Pressure in Design
Atomic and Molecular Mass in Everyday Products
Rates of Chemical Reactions in Everyday Life
Relationships among Pressure, Volume, and Temperature

competencies.text: identify Filipino and international physicists and explain how their discoveries contribute to technologies used in everyday life;

identify and explore various career paths and opportunities related to Physics (e.g. Medical Physics, Biophysics, Nuclear Physics, Meteorology, Space Science, Data Science, Materials Science, Engineering, and Energy Studies);

describe the connected concepts of circular and rotational motion in everyday life, such as satellite motion, amusement park rides, and safety practices in driving cars and handling industrial machines;
describe how aerodynamic objects such as umbrellas, roofs and airplane wings behave in situations with unequal air speeds and air pressures;
gather information through secondary sources how aerodynamic vehicles and structures are designed based on the effects of airspeed and air pressure;
explore the applications of color mixing with pigments and light in industries such as art, entertainment, photography, engineering, and food production;
investigate the phenomenon of wave interference in water ripples, vibrating guitar strings, sound amplifiers; and overlapping radio signals; and
use secondary sources to discuss applications of wave interference in technologies such as noise canceling devices, holography, and anti-reflection coatings.

explain the significance of calculating atomic mass, formula mass, and molecular mass in everyday applications such as nutrition labeling, pharmaceutical dosage formulation, and chemical product development;
explain the mole concept in counting particles of a substance and describe its applications in medicine, environmental monitoring, and industry including pharmaceuticals and pollution monitoring;

investigate how factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions, such as surface area and temperature, influence real-life applications, including cooking, food spoilage, drug efficacy and the shelf life of consumer products;
describe different organic compounds that can be found at home and in school and their role in consumer products, industry, health and medicine;
explain how specific organic compounds contribute to environmental issues such as air pollution and climate change; and

conduct observations and interpret data to describe how changes in: a. pressure affects the volume of a gas, b. temperature affects the volume of a gas, and c. temperature affects the pressure of gas.
